one_line: Council-service workspace where an agent adapts the interface and drafts housing repairs while the resident remains in control.
what_it_does: Lets residents use natural language to adapt a council-services UI, prepare a housing-repair request, review it, and submit only after human confirmation; the persisted repair then appears in staff workflow.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP materially enables shared human-agent state: the agent can adapt the live interface and update the same repair draft the resident sees, with a deliberate human-only submission boundary.
leverage_evidence: About text describes six structured tools and the same live housing-repair draft visible and editable by the resident.
About text claims 11/11 natural-language tool-selection and safety scenarios passed.
Frame sheet shows a WebMCP interaction panel and page state, but visible failure states limit certainty.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent resident-to-staff workflow with safety gating and persistence, but end-to-end execution is claimed rather than demonstrated by a submitted video.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and the description specifies draft, confirmation, submission, reference generation, and staff inbox persistence.
Frame evidence shows the product UI and WebMCP panel, though the contact sheet appears to include error states.
No video transcript or actual video is supplied.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete accessibility and public-service problem for residents with varied abilities and preferences, while preserving human agency over consequential submission.
impact_evidence: Description identifies council-service accessibility barriers and a resident/staff repair use case.
The workflow supports larger text, larger controls, simpler language, and stepwise completion.
creativity_rationale: The human-agent collaboration model treats adaptive interface presentation and shared state as the product, rather than merely adding an agent button to a form.
creativity_evidence: Pitch centers Humans × Agents and agent adaptation of the same resident-facing interface.
Human-only confirmation and staff-side persisted reference are integrated into the concept.
usability_note: The stated adaptive controls and review gate are strong, though visible contact-sheet errors reduce confidence in polish.
red_flags: No submitted video despite frame-sheet artifacts; contact sheet appears to show failed interactions.
Execution and final persistence are primarily claimed.
standouts: Shared live state between resident and agent.
Human-only final submission with staff inbox continuity.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-specific shared-state and accessibility concept with credible impact; advance despite limited execution evidence.

one_line: Evidence-first memory layer that preserves human observations and exposes carefully classified knowledge to agents.
what_it_does: Accepts natural-language observations, preserves the confirmed source, lets the human review subject and text, derives semantic relations with epistemic labels, and exposes confirmed memory through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: The structured agent surface is central: it gives agents queryable, provenance-preserving memory while separating human evidence from agent inference, a capability general UI driving cannot reproduce comparably reliably.
leverage_evidence: Description defines Human context → Confirmed memory → WebMCP → Agent reasoning.
Relations distinguish SOURCE_EXPLICIT, SOURCE_STRONGLY_IMPLIED, and AGENT_INFERRED.
Human confirmation is required before memory becomes authoritative.
execution_rationale: The model and workflow are unusually coherent, but the packet lacks a video and provides limited visible proof of the complete lifecycle.
execution_evidence: Description specifies capture, review, confirmation, semantic discovery, classification, and querying.
Frame sheet visibly shows evidence-capture and review/confirm states.
No transcript or submitted video is supplied.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real weakness in AI systems: missing, unstructured, and silently distorted human context, with value for teams and individuals relying on durable agent memory.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies observations, decisions, hypotheses, and experience as valuable context currently trapped in unstructured forms.
Provenance and unknown-state handling directly mitigate misleading agent reasoning.
creativity_rationale: The evidence/epistemology boundary and explicit ownership split between human source and agent reasoning are a distinctive interaction and data model.
creativity_evidence: Two-stage semantic construction separates candidate relation discovery from epistemic classification.
The concept preserves what was actually said instead of collapsing it into model-generated facts.
usability_note: Natural-language capture plus review/confirm is approachable; the epistemic model may add complexity.
red_flags: End-to-end WebMCP query evidence is not clearly visible in the supplied contact sheet.
standouts: Strong provenance and epistemic classification model.
advance_reason: Highly differentiated agent-memory concept with strong WebMCP leverage and credible usefulness.

one_line: Browser-based front-end editor where agents write code and immediately inspect accessibility and compatibility results.
what_it_does: Combines multi-file editing, live preview, WCAG auditing, responsive preview, design-token checks, and browser compatibility inspection behind a WebMCP surface.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP closes the edit-preview-audit loop in one shared surface, making agent-generated code directly inspectable and correctable without fragile tab orchestration.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly exposes editor, preview, and WCAG audit to browser agents.
Description says every preview refresh runs accessibility checks and violations include exact elements and fixes.
Video metadata is misleading (Rick Astley title), weakening evidence trust.
execution_rationale: The described scope is substantial and coherent, but the packet has no public repo and the supplied video metadata is clearly inconsistent, so execution evidence is capped.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive.
Description specifies concrete editor, preview, audit, responsive, design-system, and compatibility features.
Video title is an unrelated music video and no transcript is provided.
impact_rationale: Front-end developers have a clear recurring problem: accessibility and design-system regressions across disconnected tools; integrating checks into the authoring loop has credible value.
impact_evidence: Description identifies editor/browser/DevTools/a11y-checker handoff friction.
WCAG and contrast checks are positioned as part of normal iteration.
creativity_rationale: This is a strong synthesis of AI coding, live preview, accessibility auditing, and design-token enforcement, though the category is established.
creativity_evidence: DESIGN.md is treated as a source of truth and drift is flagged in AI-written CSS.
The agent is given the same editor and audit context.
usability_note: One-tab workflow is compelling, but evidence does not establish polish or reliability.
red_flags: Video title points to unrelated content, making video evidence unusable.
standouts: Accessibility audit integrated into the agent coding loop.
advance_reason: Good concept and claimed feature breadth, but the packet's video evidence is invalid and execution cannot be established.

one_line: Marketplace where buyer and seller agents negotiate a multidimensional deal before a human confirms purchase.
what_it_does: Provides storefront tools for search, cart, add-ons, coupons, and multi-round negotiation, with economic constraints enforced and human confirmation required before buying.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables page-local buyer/seller tool discovery and structured multi-turn negotiation against live commerce state; generic UI driving would be markedly less reliable for this interaction.
leverage_evidence: Description says every storefront page registers search, cart, add-on, coupon, and negotiation tools.
Buyer and store agents haggle over price, quantity, freebies, shipping, and coupons.
Nothing is purchased until the human confirms.
execution_rationale: The packet specifies a coherent marketplace, agent loop, shared state, single mutation path, and economic invariants; visual evidence should support a high claimed-execution score.
execution_evidence: Demo is alive and repository is public.
Backend architecture uses OffersService.applyTurn as the sole negotiation transition path.
Description claims 95k+ products and a visible confirm dialog.
impact_rationale: It targets a clear desire to delegate shopping research and bargaining without surrendering purchase authority, with value for price-sensitive shoppers.
impact_evidence: Pitch and description identify the trust barrier around autonomous purchasing.
Budget/floor constraints and human confirmation directly address that barrier.
creativity_rationale: Agent-to-agent bargaining over a multidimensional offer, with a human confirmation boundary, is memorable and ambitious beyond ordinary shopping assistants.
creativity_evidence: Negotiation includes quantity, add-ons, shipping, and coupon stacking rather than just price.
Buyer and seller agents interact through page tools.
usability_note: The confirmation boundary is legible; negotiation complexity could be dense but is appropriate to the concept.
red_flags: Claims of 95k+ real products are not independently verifiable from packet alone.
standouts: Pure mutation path enforcing buyer budget and seller floor.
advance_reason: Excellent WebMCP leverage and originality with a concrete trust-preserving commerce workflow.

one_line: Business planner that turns an idea into product, pricing, launch, and marketing decisions.
what_it_does: Guides a user from a business goal through product ideas, selection, pricing, a seven-day launch plan, and a generated marketing kit with human decisions.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools package a familiar planning workflow and may improve repeatability, but the packet does not establish that WebMCP changes the capability substantially versus an agent using the UI.
leverage_evidence: Description claims a structured Goal → Product → Price → Launch → Marketing workflow.
Agent activity is shown as part of the experience.
No frame sheets were submitted, so tool/state behavior cannot be checked.
execution_rationale: The scope is understandable but evidence is thin: no video frames, and the supplied about text is heavily malformed/truncated.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and six gallery images are listed.
Description enumerates outputs but does not demonstrate completion end to end.
No video frame sheets submitted.
impact_rationale: Aspiring digital-product sellers are identifiable and the outputs are useful, but fit and quality of generated recommendations are not demonstrated.
impact_evidence: Packet names a concrete audience and business-planning sequence.
Outputs include price, launch plan, and marketing assets.
creativity_rationale: A competent synthesis of AI business planning with a human-in-the-loop workflow, without a clearly novel interaction model in the packet.
creativity_evidence: Combines product, price, launch, and marketing generation.
Human makes final decisions.
usability_note: The linear workflow sounds approachable, but no visual evidence was available to assess usability.
red_flags: About text is malformed and evidence is largely descriptive.
advance_reason: Potentially useful but insufficient evidence and limited demonstrated WebMCP differentiation.

one_line: Browser extension that lets agents make safe, reversible, persistent webpage personalizations.
what_it_does: Agents inspect pages and apply validated plans to change styles, hide or move elements, add safe components, create shortcuts, and remember preferences across visits.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives an agent a constrained, structured control surface over arbitrary webpages while preserving target freshness, atomicity, rollback, and human confirmation; generic UI driving cannot match the safety and repeatability.
leverage_evidence: Tools include inspect_page and apply_page_plan with opaque short-lived target IDs.
Plans are validated atomically with fingerprints, navigation checks, and target revalidation.
Changes are local, reversible, and persistent.
execution_rationale: The safety architecture and lifecycle are detailed and coherent, with a plausible completed extension workflow; frame evidence supports the interface but not every edge case.
execution_evidence: Demo is alive and repository is public.
Description specifies confirmation, cancellation, rollback, persistence, and dynamic shortcuts.
Frame sheets show browser UI and tool interaction states.
impact_rationale: It addresses a broad and real accessibility and personalization gap: users can adapt sites they do not control to their own needs and workflows.
impact_evidence: Packet names styles, accessibility, element visibility/movement, shortcuts, and persistent preferences.
Works on websites the user does not own.
creativity_rationale: Safe agent-mediated personalization of arbitrary third-party webpages, using ephemeral target capabilities instead of arbitrary code, is a novel and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Opaque one-use snapshots and revalidation turn page editing into a constrained plan application.
Supports both extensions and built-in agent browsers.
usability_note: Reversible plans and confirmation support trust; the target-plan model may be technical for end users.
red_flags: OpenRouter fallback implies an alternate access path; WebMCP remains the primary claimed integration.
Some extension/browser compatibility claims are not independently observed.
standouts: Persistent personalization across sites without arbitrary JS/CSS injection.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-leverage WebMCP capability with credible user value and strong safety design.

one_line: Storefront where agents can research and prepare purchases but checkout appears only after scoped human approval.
what_it_does: Lets users state shopping rules, agents search and compare products, fill a cart and delivery details, and request approval; checkout is dynamically exposed only when the exact basket, address, and rules are approved.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the authorization mechanism: tool availability itself changes with approval and live page state, making the no-checkout-until-approved guarantee stronger than an agent merely receiving a refusal.
leverage_evidence: Checkout is absent from the agent toolbox until human approval.
Approval binds to a particular cart and address and is revoked when either changes.
Agent and human operate on the same cart in the same tab.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a focused, internally consistent shopping and authorization workflow with explicit invariants; repository/demo evidence is present.
execution_evidence: Demo is alive and repository is public.
Description specifies seventeen tools, rule checks, delivery completeness, approval, and dynamic tool exposure.
The workflow has a clear final state and revalidation behavior.
impact_rationale: It tackles a real trust and safety barrier to delegated commerce while retaining the convenience of agent research and cart preparation.
impact_evidence: Description identifies that users will delegate research but not purchase.
Budget, address, and exact-basket approval create a concrete safety mechanism.
creativity_rationale: Making authority a live capability boundary—checkout does not exist until a scoped approval—is a memorable interaction model with strong conceptual clarity.
creativity_evidence: The agent has nothing to retry or argue with because checkout is not registered.
Approval is cryptographically/scopingly tied in the described UI state to basket and address.
usability_note: Plain-language rules and visible agent actions make delegation understandable; exception handling is only claimed.
red_flags: No submitted video frame sheets were available for direct checking beyond the packet's claimed evidence.
advance_reason: One of the clearest demonstrations of WebMCP changing safety semantics, with a compelling commerce use case.

one_line: Investigation workspace where agents analyze uploaded datasets and build visible, evidence-linked explanations.
what_it_does: Supports CSV upload, agent-led investigations, queries, group comparisons, charts, evidence recording, activity timelines, investigation graphs, and summaries.
leverage_rationale: Structured investigation tools and visible activity/evidence state can make agent data exploration more repeatable and auditable than generic UI driving, though the packet does not establish indispensability.
leverage_evidence: Description lists tools for starting investigations, querying, comparing groups, creating charts, and recording insights.
Agent activity timeline and Investigation Graph expose intermediate state.
No frame sheets were submitted.
execution_rationale: The concept is coherent but execution evidence is thin: no video frames and the about page contains many empty sections.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and two gallery images are listed.
Description enumerates a full investigation workflow.
No video frame sheets submitted; packaging text has empty headings.
impact_rationale: Data analysts and decision-makers have a clear need for exploratory analysis that explains evidence and reasoning, though demonstrated usefulness is not available.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies CSV investigation, pattern discovery, visualization, and evidence tracking.
Final summaries and history support reviewability.
creativity_rationale: The investigation graph and evidence-building workflow are a fresh synthesis beyond ordinary chart generation, but the underlying category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent actions are represented in an activity timeline and Investigation Graph.
The product emphasizes stepwise evidence rather than only a final answer.
usability_note: Visual investigation history could help users understand agent work, but usability cannot be assessed without frames.
red_flags: Several empty Devpost sections and limited execution proof.
standouts: Visible agent activity rather than opaque answer generation.
advance_reason: Solid idea, but the packet lacks enough execution evidence to justify advancing over better-supported projects.

one_line: Privacy-preserving browser reading room for agent-assisted volumetric CT and MRI exploration.
what_it_does: Loads local or bundled NIfTI studies, renders 3D volumes, lets agents describe studies, find bright regions, focus findings, change layouts, and export only with human approval.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes structured measurements and navigation controls while keeping the scan in-browser; the agent can assist without receiving sensitive pixel data, a major capability and privacy delta over ordinary UI driving or hosted upload.
leverage_evidence: Five tools return measurements/metadata while the agent never receives the scan.
Only export_findings moves data off-page and requires explicit human approval.
Description states agents can update visible overlays on the image.
execution_rationale: The product scope, technical stack, privacy boundary, and tool behavior are coherent and specific; the packet includes visual frame evidence though no video transcript.
execution_evidence: Demo is alive and repository is public.
Description specifies local NIfTI loading, NiiVue rendering, five tools, overlays, and approval-gated export.
Three frame sheets are supplied for visual product evidence.
impact_rationale: It addresses a high-stakes, concrete need in medical imaging: useful agent assistance without sending patient scans to a hosted model.
impact_evidence: Packet directly identifies hospital privacy constraints around MRI/CT uploads.
Local browser processing and metadata-only agent responses reduce exposure while preserving assistance.
creativity_rationale: Combining volumetric medical imaging, privacy-preserving local computation, and agent navigation through structured tools is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Agent can find and focus bright regions in a volumetric reading room without seeing the scan.
Human-approved export is integrated into the privacy model.
usability_note: The reading-room metaphor and overlays are promising; medical workflows and 3D navigation can still be demanding.
red_flags: Clinical usefulness and diagnostic validity are not established; should not be treated as a medical device claim.
standouts: Agent assistance without transmitting scan pixels.
advance_reason: Exceptional privacy-aware WebMCP leverage, high-stakes impact, and ambitious technical concept.

one_line: Life-event paperwork hub that derives one canonical profile and coordinates approved filings across multiple portals.
what_it_does: Turns a natural-language life event into facts, deadlines, portal-specific drafts, conflict reconciliation, human-reviewed submissions, and receipts across agencies, insurers, and employers.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic per-portal tool registration and structured cross-portal state make multi-site paperwork coordination substantially more reliable than a general agent clicking disconnected forms.
leverage_evidence: Each portal dynamically registers tools only while the agent is on that page.
A canonical profile feeds drafts and a reconciliation engine catches conflicts across portals.
Every write is a two-call human approval gate and produces a receipt.
execution_rationale: The workflow is unusually complete on paper, with deadline math, reconciliation, approval, and receipts; visual evidence supports the product but does not prove every portal integration.
execution_evidence: Demo is alive and six gallery images are listed.
Description specifies a concrete birth/dependent example and three independent portals.
Three frame sheets are supplied; no transcript is provided.
impact_rationale: It targets a pervasive, high-friction life-admin problem with deadlines and repeated data entry, and preserves human approval over consequential filings.
impact_evidence: Packet cites 15–40 actions after a major life event and real enrollment deadlines.
Cross-portal conflict detection and one-sentence entry directly address errors and burden.
creativity_rationale: The cross-portal paperwork orchestration model, with capability scoped to the current page and human-approved receipts, is ambitious and distinctive.
creativity_evidence: One canonical profile is reconciled against independent portal representations.
Tool surfaces appear/disappear with page context via AbortController.
usability_note: One-sentence intake and plain-language reconciliation reduce burden; multi-portal exceptions remain a risk.
red_flags: Actual external portal filing cannot be fully verified from packet evidence.
advance_reason: High-impact, highly differentiated WebMCP orchestration with strong safety and evidence-aware workflow design.
